raw_response:
I've been working this land since I was a young man, following what my father did, and what his father did before him. Here in Quzhou, everyone grows wheat and corn — that's just how it is. The soil is flat, the wells are there for irrigation, and the grain merchants come every harvest. I don't need to think too hard about this. I know what works.

My land is about 12 mu. I'll split it even — six mu wheat in winter, six mu corn in summer, same as every year. No point changing.

For wheat, I'll buy seed from Lao Zhang's shop in the village — he always stocks that Jimai variety, the one with the good stalks that don't fall over. For corn, Zhengdan 958. Everyone uses it. The yield is reliable and I know how it behaves in drought.

Fertilizer — I put down compound fertilizer at planting, then top up with urea when the wheat is jointing. For corn I do the same at the big bell stage. My neighbor Wei told me his wheat was thin last year because he used too little urea. I'd rather spend a bit more and not worry. My son says I use too much, but he doesn't farm.

I'll irrigate wheat three times — once in November before winter, once at jointing in March, once at heading. Corn gets two — at tasseling and grain fill if it doesn't rain.

I plow with the rotary tiller after harvest before wheat. For corn I go straight into the stubble after wheat — less work, the soil is already loose.
